paper.title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Wind Farm Layouts—Complexity, Constraint Handling and Scalability

checked: paper body, acknowledgements, references and PDF annotations
GitHub exact MOGOMEA and o-MOGOMEA searches
public_source_audit.resolution: clean-room paper-equation reconstruction with every completion declared

paper_native_problem.encoding: binary occupancy of square candidate grids
paper_native_problem.turbine: Vestas V164-8 MW, diameter 164 m, hub height 107 m, Table-3 power and thrust values with linear interpolation
paper_native_problem.wind: Table-4 twelve direction-specific mean speeds and annual frequencies
paper_native_problem.wake: Katic-Jensen with offshore roughness 0.0005 m, thrust-dependent deficit, partial rotor overlap and root-sum-square combination
paper_native_problem.objectives: maximize normalized expected wind-farm energy and installed-turbine efficiency

paper_native_methods: MOGOMEA with five objective-space clusters, online mutual-information linkage trees, GOM, FI, two single-objective extreme clusters, archive and population growth
o-MOGOMEA with the same framework and one geographic-distance offline linkage tree
NSGA-II with two-point crossover 0.9, bit-flip probability 1/l, archive and evaluation-equivalent population growth
c-NSGA-II with the same NSGA-II and within-objective-cluster mating
constraint_handlers: constraint domination without evaluating infeasible offspring
one-ideal-turbine energy penalty per violating pair
randomly remove one turbine per conflict until feasible
up to 100 resampling attempts followed by parent/subset fallback
missing_information: author Python source and random states
exact mutual-information normalization, UPGMA tie rules and cluster ties
numeric base NIS and hypervolume history implementation
machine-readable Pareto fronts, layouts, convergence arrays and timings
conflicts_and_completions: Interpret Table-4 directions as meteorological wind-from and convert to flow-to.
Use binary mutual information in nats normalized by ln(2), average-link UPGMA and stable variable-index ties online; use Euclidean site distance under identical UPGMA rules offline.
Infer tau=0.5 exactly from c=(2/k)floor(tau*n), k=5, n=20 and stated initial cluster size c=4.
Use an unbounded archive modulo identical layouts/objectives because the paper only says it was large enough for every nondominated layout.
Use the explicit FI threshold 1+floor(log10(n)) as the missing NIS window and 2*NIS as the fixed-resolution stop.
At multi-resolution stages keep the 8D mutation probability, map old sites exactly and initialize new variables to zero.
Use paper-observed best CHTs for Figure-17 roles: repair for MOGOMEA, resample for o-MOGOMEA and constraint domination for both NSGA-II variants.
Preserve all four CHT labels at 8D because Figs. 13-15 report that full matrix even though no conflicts can occur.

paper_protocol.fixed_role_derivation: four algorithms times four farms times three grid steps times four active CHT labels
paper_protocol.physical_fes_interpretation: one complete layout objective evaluation yields both objectives and counts once even though the paper says per objective
paper_protocol.target_only_boundary: the four algorithms studied and modified in Sections 3.3-3.6 are targets; algorithms only cited in Table 1 are excluded

hpc.precomputation: coordinates, conflict pairs, wind rotations, ideal powers, power/thrust arrays and offline linkage are immutable
hpc.evaluator: one complete layout is serial inside a population task; layouts are fixed-index parallel, while isolated-layout validation is parallel over twelve wind states
hpc.algorithm: offspring construction, individual GOM trajectories, dominance rows and five online linkage trees are parallel over a persistent all-core team
hpc.sequential_boundaries: one GOM trajectory, archive commit order, population growth, resolution transfer and hypervolume history
hpc.required_invariant: one-worker and all-worker objective, physical FES, final archive and scientific hash identity

claim_boundary: Flexible equation-level academic reproduction of all twelve fixed-resolution problems, four target algorithms, four active CHTs and multi-resolution roles; not author Python, exact absent implementation choices, random stream, numerical fronts, convergence trajectories or hardware timing replay.
